rubric: FROM ASSEMBLER TO C / ABSTRACTIONS IN C / CHAPTER 7

slides.title: What the preprocessor does
slides.main: The preprocessor substitutes text before compilation; gcc -E shows the result.

captions: Before compilation the preprocessor runs: it reads text and emits new text, substituting one thing for another
It knows no types, functions, or variables; in assembler, macros and the include directive were similar
gcc -E stops after the preprocessor and shows the text the compiler will get

slides.title: #include and headers
slides.main: A header holds declarations; a .c file holds definitions.

captions: #include literally copies the file's contents in place of the directive
<…> searches system headers, "…" looks next to your file first
Headers hold declarations: prototypes, types, constants; function definitions live in a single .c

frames.text: agreement and implementation — in different files

captions: A file includes two headers, and both include a third — the struct is defined twice: error
Include guard: if the macro is already defined, skip the text; otherwise define it and read
First time the text enters the file, second time it is dropped; #pragma once is shorter, but the guard works everywhere

slides.title: #define without parameters
slides.main: No type or address: enum and const are better.

captions: #define NAME text replaces the name everywhere below in the file until #undef
Such a constant has no type, address, or scope, and the debugger can't see it — it gets a plain number
A set of integers is better as enum, a single typed constant as const; a macro is needed only when you need text

slides.title: Macros with parameters
slides.main: Parentheses around parameters and around the whole body.

captions: SQ(x) as x * x: SQ(a + 1) gives a + 1 * a + 1 — not a square
Put every parameter in the body in parentheses: ((x) * (x))
And the whole body too: otherwise neighbors merge — 100 / SQ(2) becomes 100 / 2 * 2

slides.title: Side effects
slides.main: static inline instead of expression macros.

captions: MAX(a, b) writes the argument twice in the body: MAX(i++, j) increments i twice
Better a static inline function: it has a type, the argument is evaluated once, and the compiler still inlines the body
For several types — the typeof extension with temporaries, or type selection via _Generic from C11

lines: static inline int max_int(int a, int b) {

slides.title: do { } while (0)
slides.main: A macro is one statement; the caller adds the semicolon.

captions: A two-statement macro in an if without braces expands so that the second statement lands outside the condition
The do { … } while (0) wrapper makes a set of actions one statement; the loop runs exactly once and vanishes under optimization
No semicolon inside the macro: the caller adds it — the call looks like a function call

lines: #define SWAP(a, b) t = a; a = b; b = t
// if (x>y) t = x;   a = b; b = t;

slides.title: # and ##
slides.main: Two macro levels to substitute a value.

captions: # turns an argument into a string literal: print an expression's text together with its value
## pastes two fragments into one name: CAT(f, 1) gives f1
If the argument is itself a macro, # and ## don't expand it; to substitute the value you need an outer macro over an inner one

slides.title: Predefined macros
slides.main: A log with the call site filled in automatically.

captions: __FILE__ — file name, __LINE__ — line number, __func__ — current function name (a predefined identifier, not a macro)
A log is built from them: the macro fills in the call site itself, no need to write it by hand
__DATE__ and __TIME__ record build time, __STDC_VERSION__ — the enabled standard: 201112L means C11

slides.title: Conditional compilation
slides.main: Build flags switch pieces of code.

captions: #if, #ifdef, #elif, #else, #endif turn pieces of text on and off; defined(X) asks whether a name is defined
The -DDEBUG flag defines the macro at build time without editing the source: debug printing in one build, none in another
#if 0 temporarily switches off a section — C has no nested comments; but keep branches to a minimum
The ellipsis in parameters and __VA_ARGS__ in the body pass the remaining arguments on — printf wrappers
X macro: items are written once as X(...) calls, then different definitions of X are substituted
One definition gives an enum, another a name table: the lists cannot drift apart

slides.title: What to choose
slides.main: Macro — for what is otherwise impossible.

captions: A number — enum or const; a computation — static inline; leave macros for what is otherwise impossible: pasting, stringification, conditional compilation
The classic macro: array size — whole size divided by element size; works only for real arrays
See the result via gcc -E and enable -Wall -Wextra: warnings catch many errors before running

frames.text: gives nonsense for a pointer: sizeof p is the pointer's size

slides.title: Summary
slides.main: Next — input and output: stdio and buffering.

captions: The preprocessor is a text-substitution pass: include copies, define replaces, conditional directives choose pieces
Headers: declarations plus a guard; parenthesize macro parameters and body; avoid side effects; multi-statement — do-while(0)
# and ## make macros stronger than functions but cost readability; next — input and output: stdio, formatting, and buffering
